chunks: Sulayman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayyub al-Lakhmi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, saying: Manjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah al-Tha'labi narrated from Ziyad ibn 'Ilqah, from Jabir ibn Samurah al-Saw'i, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"I asked my Lord, Blessed and Exalted, for three things, and He granted me two and withheld one. I said: 'O Lord, do not destroy my nation with hunger.' He said: 'This is for you.' I said: 'O Lord, do not place upon them an enemy from among others, meaning the polytheists, so they may devastate them.' He said: 'This is for you.' I said: 'O Lord, do not make their conflict among themselves,' so He withheld this one."
Sulayman ibn Ahmad said: 'This hadith is not narrated from Ali (peace be upon him) except through this chain; Manjab ibn al-Harith alone narrated it.'

key_terms.تَفَرَّدَ بِهِ: he was unique in narrating it

ai.seo_question: What three things did the Prophet ask God for regarding his nation, and which one was withheld?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal highlights the Prophet’s intercession for his Ummah, emphasizing that while divine protection from famine and external conquest was secured, internal discord (fitnah) was left as a test of faith. The specific chain of transmission, unique to Manjab ibn al-Harith, underscores the careful scrutiny of narrators in Shia scholarship to preserve the authenticity of this theological insight. It reflects the Shia understanding of historical events, particularly the civil wars, as a divinely permitted trial rather than a failure of divine promise.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-9 Suleiman ibn Ahmad ibn Ayoob al-Lakhmy narrated that Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shoyba’ quoted Minjab ibn al-Harith, on the authority of Abu Hozayfah al-Sa’labi, on the authority of Zyad ibn Alaqa, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah al-Sava’ee, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“I asked my Lord - the Blessed the Sublime - for three things. He granted me two of them, but did not grant me the third. I said, ‘O Lord! Please do not let my nation be destroyed by hunger’. The Lord said, ‘Let it be so.’ I said, ‘O Lord! Please do not let their enemies - that is the polytheists - take over my nation so as to uproot my people.’ The Lord said, ‘Let it be so.’ I said, ‘O Lord! Please do not let there be any mischief amongst them.’ The Lord did not grant me this.”
Suleiman ibn Ahmad said, “There have been no other chains of narration of this tradition from Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB). Only Minjab ibn al-Harith has narrated it.”
